description: Creates an outgoing webhook or changes one you already have: what it fires on, where it delivers, how, and which fields it maps or filters. Take it when another system should hear about registrations, attendance or purchases: "Send every buyer to my CRM." It needs the session, and on a new one a trigger and the address your other system gave you. A webhook fires for every webinar on your site, not only this one, so that belongs in one sentence before anything is saved. A test copy address is readable by anyone with the link and switches itself off after a few hours, so it is never the real destination. Turning it on needs an active plan, exactly like the form. Side effect: it acts on your connected WordPress site; nothing else is touched. Words hosts use: webhook, send to CRM, Zapier, connect my tool, registration trigger

active.description: true turns it on so it really fires. Default is saved but silent.

conditions.description: Field mapping and conditions: [{field, operator, value?, field_name?, field_value?}].

mirror_url.description: An optional test copy address. Anyone with that link can read what is sent, and it turns itself off after a few hours. An empty string removes it.

name.description: The label in the webhook list. Auto-named from the trigger when left out on create.

secret.description: An optional signing secret the receiving system gave the host. Never guessed.

session_id.description: From an earlier turn (weiter · texte · stand).

site.description: Which connected site is meant when this chat has more than one: the address exactly as wi_get_connector_status lists it under sites. Leave it out while only one site is connected.

trigger.description: What makes it fire. Needed on create.

url.description: The receiving system's own delivery address. Needed on create, never invented.

webhook_id.description: 0 or left out creates a new webhook, an id changes that one.

name: wi_save_webhook
title: Save an outgoing webhook
